hook_text: By the end of this sheet, someone who has never met you could build your crane. That is what a working drawing is.
clip_script: Landscape sheet, border, title block: team, name, date, scale 1:2, millimetres. Table of halves on scrap paper. Now grow the crane. Base first: a flat parallelogram, sides at 45 degrees. Mast standing on it, tall and thin. Arm across from the top. A little circle at the tip with centre lines: the pulley. Thin line down: the string. Nail with a coil band: the magnet. Winch at the foot: drum, axle dashed where it hides, handle. Cells at the back as a counterweight. Light lines, then dark edges. Sizes once each, real numbers, nothing crossing. Circle the winch, call it A, draw it bigger in the corner with its own scale. Now hand it to a team mate and say: build it. Every question they ask is a fix.
visual_style: Whiteboard sheet with border and title block; base parallelogram, mast, arm, pulley, magnet, winch appearing in order; dimension lines landing; a circle labelled A expanding into a detail.
mood: Methodical and satisfying, a drawing assembling itself.
pacing: Sheet, table, base, mast, arm, tip, winch, sizes, detail, handover, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your crane so a stranger could build it.
